2. The short fact leading to this Rule is that, the petitioner and two opposite parties are full-brothers and they constructed a tin-shed house at 28 Shantibagh Road, Dhaka and when the plaintiff requested his two other brothers for partition of all of their properties it was refused which resulted in the filing of the suit for partition. In that suit the defendants entered appearance and the parties compromised the suit and the same was decreed in terms of a solenama and for effecting sole-decree an Advocate Commissioner was appointed who after executing the commission submitted a report against which the petitioner filed an objection which was on hearing rejected by the learned Subordinate Judge, Additional Court, Dhaka and he accepted the report. The petitioner on being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the Commissioner''s report moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 3. Mr Syed Mokaddas Ali, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the original suit for partition was decreed on compromise and the solenama filed was made a part of the decree and a commissioner was deputed from the Court to effect partition by metes and bounds. But while distributing the saham the Advocate Commissioner admittedly left certain properties and also has not taken proper measurement of the lands is question. He also admittedly kept out a pond and its banks out of partition and also has not partitioned the village properties. The learned Advocate contends that such partition cannot be piecemeal. He also submits that the Commissioner has given more Dhaka lands to opposite parties 1 and 2 which is inconsistent with the decree passed and no explanation has been given by the Commissioner why he has given more land than the due lands to the opposite parties. The learned Advocate contends that the measurement of Dhaka properties given by the Commissioner is also vague and indefinite and the Commissioner''s report is not at all satisfactory by which the partition cannot be effected. Against this the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties submits that the report of the Advocate Commissioner indicates that he has given more Dhaka land to the opposite parties and this may be due to effecting partition.
